## GATE1 · GATE1-trace-ring — GATE1 on K20: the rv32 gate's trace ring overflows (dropped 22,532)

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 13

Evidence: Ruled by the Architect in three steps: (a) one ring of 16384 pages for both widths; then (c) the cause before the size, which GATE1's diagnosis found in the frame allocator's first-fit scan (every alloc_frame scans past the ring's frames, billed to the caller: mean scan 8806 -&gt; 16997 slots; churn shell 499 -&gt; 559; R10 flat; audits unbilled) - a production term linear in RAM frames against R12, cut as K21; and for GATE1 the ring's frames taken from the top of RAM so the object frames below sit where a release kernel's do. Built at 3340374d7: churn shell 498/504, gate fill 31% rv64 / 35% rv32 of 2,097,152 (memory_mib stays 256), every lease filled its table, notice p99 25829/26195, R10 22376/22368; the 288 MiB control run showed the record count follows the ring's position, not free RAM. Whole bench alone 283 PASS, 1 SKIP, 0 FAIL. Page line on scheduling.md's 'Measured on QEMU, on one hart'. The bench build race found on the way is B7.

Event: `e21a8a4421f0fb2eefb508ae5139dba2` · 2026-10-03T03:42:40Z

> Ruling: (a), one ring size for both widths, and GATE1 carries it.
> 
> - The ring doubles: trace::PAGES 8192 -> 16384, which is 64 MiB and 2^21 records of 32 bytes. That is one constant in sched.rs's trace module, compiled only under sched-trace. rv32's kernel half is no limit: its physmap is about 2 GiB, and the ring is kernel frames taken at boot before the budget tree. Today's overflow is 2.1% (1,071,108 records needed against 1,048,576), so doubling leaves about half the ring free on rv32. Keep one size, not one per width: a width-dependent trace shape is a second thing to keep right.
> - The cost is RAM. The traced cases boot with 256 MiB, and the budget tree gets 64 MiB less instead of 32. The implementer checks that kernel-containment's leases still fill their handle tables before their pages run out, and that every other traced case is green on both widths. If any is short of RAM, that case sets memory_mib, a case-file line, rather than shrinking the ring.
> - GATE1's report records each width's ring fill in the gate, as records used of 2,097,152, so the headroom is on record. The bench already fails on any drop, so the rule stays "dropped 0".
> - (b) is refused. The direct billing check is most useful exactly in the gate's full fill: a hostile load is where a stale wait or a timer tail would land on a victim. Two trace shapes would also mean two oracles' expectations.
> - (c) and (d) are refused, for the reasons you give.
> 
> Page line, in GATE1's commit: scheduling.md "Residual risks", the "Measured on QEMU, on one hart" bullet. Change "and 32 MiB less RAM for the budget tree" to "and 64 MiB less RAM for the budget tree". The constant's doc comment in sched.rs moves with it ("Frames the ring takes (64 MiB)").
> 
> Whose: GATE1's. It is the package that needs the room, the change is test-only, and K20 is merged. A follow-up package for one constant would be all overhead.

Event: `7a77a8ce9a1d84a5010933d21042f081` · 2026-10-03T04:53:26Z

> Ruling: a kernel finding, so K21. GATE1 takes (ii) and merges without waiting for K21.
> 
> K21 (todo, Tier A, M, no needs). Brief and page lines: .wash/local/K21-implementer.md. R12 (scheduling.md) already settles it: "A term linear in RAM frames ... is not [a constant]. Billing it to the caller does not excuse it". Reading mem.rs, alloc_frame's first fit is one of three such scans on call paths:
> - alloc_frame: every page, page table and object frame;
> - alloc_contiguous: dma_alloc's first-fit run search;
> - release_owned_frames: process_create's rollback scans all of RAM.
> 
> The fixes:
> - an O(1) free list (intrusive through the physmap preferred), with a checked-build audit that the list equals the table's free entries;
> - the rollback walks what the creation built;
> - dma_alloc gets a fixed boot pool or a run allocator, decided in K21 or brought back to me;
> - scan-bounds is extended, with a recorded negative (alloc-first-fit).
> 
> GATE1, (ii): take the ring's frames from the top of RAM, so the object frames below sit where a release kernel's do. That is right on its own merits: a test-only region must not change the production layout it is measuring. It is a few lines in kernel_frame (sched-trace only), carried by GATE1. sched-budget-churn should return to 499; report it on both widths.
> 
> The gate's fill: the 288 MiB run still decides. If the gate's count stays above 75% of the ring with the ring on top, the gate also sets memory_mib = 288, its own case-file line. Report the fill and the sweep's worst seed with whichever lands.
> 
> Page line, in GATE1's commit: scheduling.md's "Measured on QEMU, on one hart" bullet ends "... and 64 MiB less RAM for the budget tree, taken from the top of RAM so the frames below sit where a release kernel's do." This replaces my earlier "64 MiB less RAM" line.
>
